warnings: Fix the source directionality first: ensure the inflow emitter’s normal truly points sideways toward the cabinet wall; the spray should start as a fanned sheet (not a vertical column).
Add/enable secondary particles for liquid (spray/foam/bubbles) or an auxiliary particle system for droplets at impact; this is the biggest realism gain for a burst hose.
Increase surface detail: either raise sim resolution/particle density (if feasible) or reduce meshing smoothness so the jet breaks into filaments and the pool carries higher-frequency ripples.
Strengthen impact dynamics: increase turbulence/vorticity-like behavior (where applicable) and ensure collisions are clean so splashes form at the wall and where runoff enters the pool.
Improve pool realism: add stronger localized ripples emanating from the runoff entry point; add subtle edge wetting/meniscus at the front lip and around props.
Refine shader: keep IOR near water (~1.333), add subtle depth-based absorption/tint (very light blue-green) and slight roughness variation so it doesn’t read like perfect glass.
Lighting: introduce a stronger cool rim/accent along the water surface and/or a more directional warm key to create sharper specular breaks and reveal surface motion.
If render budget allows, increase samples or use denoising tuned for refraction to reduce jagged edges and improve transparency stability.
